NKE.rationale: Nike is in its most severe operational downturn in over a decade, with fundamental deterioration across all key metrics. Q3 FY2026 showed EPS down 35% YoY on flat revenue, operating cash flow collapsed 76% YoY, and gross margin compressed 120bp. The Q4 FY2026 results (reported 2026-06-30) show early stabilization — first adjusted EPS growth in two years, gross margin ex-refund flat at 40.2%, and wholesale repair gaining traction — but this is largely driven by a one-time $986M tariff refund; adjusted EPS of $0.20 still reflects deeply depressed profitability. Net income has fallen 44% in FY2025 and another 3% in FY2026 to $3.11B, while EBITDA collapsed from $7.2B (FY2024) to $3.95B (FY2026). The structural tariff headwind of ~$1.5B annualized (~320bp gross margin drag) is permanent, and competitive erosion from On, Hoka, and New Balance is accelerating in Nike's core running and lifestyle categories. Greater China revenue fell 12% in Q4 with six consecutive quarters of decline. Valuation remains unattractive: at 29x PE, the market is paying a higher multiple for roughly half the earnings power seen nine months ago (net margin 4.8% vs 9.4%, ROE 16% vs 32%), and the 3.4% earnings yield is below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.49%, implying a negative equity risk premium. News sentiment is persistently negative (mean -0.278 over 46 articles). The Dow Jones removal risk adds further downside pressure. While Nike's brand moat remains wide (#1 apparel brand globally, Brand Strength Index 94.7/100), the turnaround is far from confirmed, and the stock offers no margin of safety at current levels for a business with declining earnings, structural tariff costs, and intensifying competition.
